📉 Learning

Loss function

In simple words

A score that measures how wrong a model's answers are; training tries to make it as small as possible.

A formula that turns all of a model's mistakes into one number, called the loss: the bigger the mistakes, the bigger the loss. Training means searching for the parameters that make the loss as small as possible.

Example. In darts, you could score each throw by its distance from the bullseye. Adding up the distances gives a loss: a better player gets a smaller number.

Lessons that teach it

  • Lesson 3: Neural Networks

Related words

  • Gradient descentA way to train a model by changing its parameters, step by step, in the direction that makes the loss smaller.
  • Learning rateA setting that controls how big a step a model takes each time it adjusts its parameters during training.
  • BackpropagationThe method a neural network uses to work out how much each weight was to blame for a mistake.
  • TrainingThe process in which a model learns from examples by making guesses and correcting its mistakes again and again.
